answers.plain:
**Subject: Eli found his voice this year. Will you help the next child find theirs?**

Dear Friend,

Last spring, a second grader named Eli sat at the back of our reading circle with his arms crossed and his eyes on the floor. When it was his turn to read aloud, he whispered, "I don't do reading."

Eli had decided, at seven years old, that books were not for him. He had fallen behind, and he knew it. So he did what many kids do when something feels impossible: he hid.

Our volunteer tutor didn't push. She slid a book across the table, one about a dog who wanted to be a firefighter, and said, "Just look at the pictures with me." The next week, Eli looked at the pictures. The week after, he read one sentence. By the end of the semester, he was reading whole pages out loud, and he asked if he could take the book home.

That book kit was the first Eli ever owned. His mother told us he read it to his little sister every night until the cover came loose.

**That is what Read Forward does.** Last year, we served 1,240 children like Eli. Each one received tutoring, encouragement, and books of their own to keep. Every one of those kids deserves the chance to say, "I do reading."

But there are more children waiting, and we need your help to reach them.

**Our goal is to raise $85,000 by December 31.** That funding will keep our tutors in classrooms, our book kits in backpacks, and our doors open to every child who needs us.

Here is what your gift can do:

- **$50 buys a book kit for one child**, a set of books to keep, read, and share with family
- **$100 gives two children** the start Eli got
- **$250 equips a whole reading group** with books for the school year

Every dollar goes toward helping a child discover that they can do this.

Please give today at **[website/donation link]**, or return the enclosed reply card with your gift in the envelope provided. If you give before December 31, you'll help us reach our goal and start the new year with every child on our list supported. [Add tax-deductibility line if applicable.]

Thank you for believing in kids like Eli. Because of you, he's not hiding anymore. He's reading ahead.

With gratitude,

**Carla Mendes**
Executive Director, Read Forward

P.S. A single $50 gift puts a book kit in a child's hands. Somewhere right now, there's a kid in the back of the room with their arms crossed, waiting for someone to slide a book across the table. Will you be that someone? [Donation link]

---

**Notes for you:**
- Eli's story is written as a plausible illustration. If it isn't a real child's story, consider labeling it as a composite or changing the name. If it is real, confirm the family's permission to share it.
- I invented details (the dog-firefighter book, the little sister, the tutor). Swap in the real ones if you have them.
- Please add your donation URL, your tax-ID or deductibility language, and the reply card details.
- I can also produce a shorter email version, a social media post, or a follow-up reminder for mid-December.

# Year-End Appeal Letter: Read Forward

**Suggested outer envelope teaser:** *Eli read his first full page out loud this year.*

---

**[Date: Mid-November 2026]**

Dear [First name],

When Eli came to us in September, he was seven years old and had gotten very good at hiding.

He sat in the back of his second-grade classroom with his chin tucked down. When it was his turn to read aloud, he asked to go to the bathroom. He wasn't being difficult. He was protecting himself from a room full of kids who could do something he couldn't yet do.

His teacher told us Eli had never owned a book. She didn't mean he'd lost one. He had never had one that was his.

So on a Tuesday afternoon, a Read Forward volunteer sat down next to him with a canvas bag and said, "This is for you. You get to keep it."

Inside were a few books chosen for his reading level and his interests (Eli, it turns out, loves anything with trucks), a notebook, and a guide for the grown-ups at home. Eli didn't say anything. He held the bag in both arms for the rest of the afternoon.

Three months later, he read a full page aloud to his class. His hand shook a little. Then he looked up, and he was grinning.

I'm telling you about Eli because he is the reason I do this work. And you are part of why he's grinning.

**Last year, Read Forward served 1,240 children.** Each one got the books, the support, and the belief that they could do this. Every one of those kids is someone's Eli.

But there are more children waiting, in classrooms where a second grader is quietly figuring out how to hide. Reading well by third grade matters. It is the point where children stop learning to read and start reading to learn. A child who falls behind then often stays behind. The good news is that it's preventable, and it starts with something as simple as a book that belongs to them.

**That's why I'm writing to you today.**

This year, we've set a goal of raising **$85,000 by December 31**. That will let us put a book kit in the hands of 1,700 children, more than we have ever reached before.

Here is what your gift does:

- **$50 buys a book kit for one child**, with books that are theirs to keep, matched to their level and interests.
- **$100 gives two children** their own bag, their own books, and their own start.
- **$250 reaches five children**, maybe a whole reading group.

Whatever you choose, please know that a gift of any size matters. A child doesn't need a fortune spent on them. They need someone to say, *this is yours, and I believe you can.*

**To give, you can:**
- Visit **[URL]** to donate securely online
- Text **[KEYWORD]** to **[NUMBER]**
- Return the enclosed reply card with a check payable to Read Forward in the envelope provided

Every gift is tax-deductible to the full extent of the law. [Optional: *Read Forward is a 501(c)(3); EIN XX-XXXXXXX.*]

I think about Eli whenever I'm tempted to believe the problem is too big. One bag. One child. One Tuesday afternoon. That's how it changes.

Thank you for being the kind of person who shows up for a kid you'll never meet. I hope you'll do it again this year.

With gratitude,

**Carla Mendes**
Executive Director, Read Forward

**P.S.** Eli's teacher told me he now asks, every single day, "Can we read today?" You can help the next child ask that question. A $50 gift buys one book kit, and your gift by December 31 helps us reach 1,700 children this year. **[URL]**

---

## Notes for you before this goes out

**Things to fix or confirm**
1. **Eli is an invented illustration.** I made up the details (trucks, the bathroom, the page read aloud, the teacher's quote). Please replace them with a real child's story, or a composite that you label as one. Get consent from the family or school, and change the name if needed. Donors lose trust fast when a story proves fabricated.
2. **Check the kit contents.** I assumed books, a notebook, and a family guide. Edit to match what you actually put in a kit.
3. **Check the third-grade claim.** It's a widely used literacy benchmark, but if you have a statistic from a source you trust, a specific number would be stronger. I left it out so as not to invent one.
4. **The goal math:** $85,000 ÷ $50 = 1,700 kits, which is 460 more children than last year. I framed it that way. If the $85,000 also covers programs or overhead, adjust the "1,700" line to avoid overpromising.
5. **Confirm the $100 and $250 tiers** and the text-to-give option. I added them as suggestions, and you may not have either set up.

**Why it's built this way**
- It opens with one child, not statistics, because donors give to a person.
- It makes "you" the hero of the story.
- It names a concrete goal and a deadline, with a tangible price, so a gift feels like it does something.
- The P.S. restates the ask, since it's often the most-read part.

**Optional additions that tend to raise response**
- **A matching gift.** If a board member or sponsor will match gifts through December 31, say so. It's usually the strongest lift available.
- **Segmented versions.** Use a "thank you for giving again" line for past donors and a softer introduction for lapsed ones.
- **A mid-December email follow-up** with a progress thermometer (e.g., "We're at $52,000 of $85,000"), and a final "last 48 hours" email on December 30–31.
- **Handwritten notes** on the top 50 or so letters.

I can adapt this into the email series, a shorter version for social, or the reply card copy if that would help.
